$comment: WHAT A DIAGNOSIS WITNESSES (kb/Work PB5597, branch review R1-1, R2-3; DESIGN-spec-conformance-review.md section 10.6),
read by lineage_reads.EvidenceTable. A conformance-suite case that a compiler is to REFUSE at an edition (a refusal
test's wiseowl/diagnostics refuse-at, a flagged case's flag at) shows a diagnosis, nothing else. It witnesses an older
rule only where what the rule asks of a compiler IS a diagnosis: its text matches none of `needs-accepting-case` (a
rule that GRANTS a form, which only a program the compiler accepts can witness; these win) AND either its catalog
`kind` is a key of `diagnosed-kinds` or its text, of any kind, matches one of `withholding-rules` (a rule that
WITHHOLDS a property from a clause, "does not imply": no accepted program can tell it was withheld, so the refusal of
a program relying on it is its one witness, kb/Work PB5783); or the next-edition rule it carries into is
declines the facility, and the read states the older text's licence to decline it, licence-<year>). Every other rule
needs a case ACCEPTED at the edition. The keys are the catalog's own `kind`s, checked against it at load.
`needs-accepting-case` is a TEXT HEURISTIC THAT FAILS CLOSED: a match sends the rule to an accepted case, so a
prohibition worded with one of these words ("may not" is excluded; "only ... may" is not) is over-refused, never
over-kept. It can miss a grant worded otherwise (a form a general format shows and no sentence states); each pattern

diagnosed-kinds.SR: a syntax rule states what a conforming program may write: a program can violate it, and the compiler satisfies it by diagnosing the violation

needs-accepting-case.why: "may be specified", "may appear": a permission, which a refusal of another form does not show
an optional element: a program omitting it must be accepted
an order left free: every order must be accepted
"can be specified": a permission in other words

withholding-rules.why: the subject is a CLAUSE or PHRASE ("This does not imply", which glosses an OCCURS DEPENDING ON rule that also states an observable result, is not taken); "use of the EXTERNAL clause does not imply that the ... name is a global name": a property withheld, which no accepted program can observe (a local declaration wins either way) and a refusal of a program that relies on it shows (kb/Work PB5783)
